transcript:
Agent: Namaste, is this Rajesh Kumar speaking?

Customer: Haan, yeh Rajesh bol raha hoon. Kaun bol raha hai?

Agent: Sir, main Priya bol rahi hoon, XYZ Finance se call kar rahi hoon. Sir, aapke account ke baare mein ek important call hai. Aapka loan account number ending in 4521 hai, aur... aur aapka EMI due tha 15th ko, Rs. 18,500 ka. Sir, abhi tak payment nahi hua. Kya aap mujhe batayenge kya situation hai?

Customer: Haan, haan, main janta hoon. Actually, Priya, mera situation bahut complicated hai abhi. <interruption> Meri wife ko accident hua tha last week, samajhte ho? Car crash tha, aur woh hospital mein hai abhi.

Agent: Oh no, sir, I'm so sorry to hear that. Kya aapki wife theek hai? Serious tha accident?

Customer: Haan, quite serious tha. Uska ek leg mein fracture tha aur uska head injury bhi tha. Toh woh ICU mein tha pehle, aab general ward mein transfer ho gayi. But, uh, the hospital bills... <interruption> the bills bahut bade hain, Priya. Lakhs mein ja rahe hain.

Agent: Sir, I completely understand. Hospital expenses bahut bade hote hain, especially ICU stay. Aapke paas kya options hain? Aapka family kisi aur se financial help le sakta hai?

Customer: Nahi, nahi. Mere paas koi family nahi yahan. Mere parents toh Lucknow mein hain, aur woh bhi bahut umar mein hain. Unhe paise bhejne mein... <interruption> main unhe burden nahi dena chahta. Aur mere salary bhi... actually, mera salary toh salary ke din ke baad check aata hai, toh abhi paisa nahi hai mere paas.

Agent: Sir, kab aapka salary credit hoga? Next week?

Customer: Haan, next week, probably 20th ko. But jab salary aayega, toh hospital ka payment pehle karna padega. Aapka EMI toh... toh mujhe thoda time chahiye. Actually, Priya, I'm really stressed about this. Meri wife abhi bhi pain mein hai aur main yahan office mein baithe-baithe uski tension le raha hoon.

Agent: Sir, main samajh sakti hoon. Yeh bahut difficult situation hai. Toh let's see... aapka outstanding balance kya hai abhi?

Customer: Aapko nahi pata? Mere paas toh statement nahi hai abhi. Main office mein hoon aur <interruption> aur phone se hi baat kar raha hoon. But mujhe lagta hai... Rs. 1,25,000 ke aas-paas baaki hai. Aur aap Rs. 18,500 bole the na?

Agent: Haan, sir, yeh sahi hai. Rs. 1,25,000 outstanding hai aur Rs. 18,500 yeh month ka EMI tha. Sir, aap samajhte ho na ki yeh payment karna zaruri hai? Aapka account already 20 days overdue ho gaya hai.

Customer: Haan, main janta hoon. But sir, <interruption> I mean, aap samajhte ho na, meri wife ki jaan important hai. Iska matlab EMI se zyada important. Main jab salary paaunga, tab main pehle hospital ka payment karunga, phir aapka payment. Kya aap mujhe ek-do mahine ka time de sakte ho?

Agent: Sir, main aapke situation ko samajhti hoon, really. Medical emergency bahut serious hota hai. Lekin mujhe aapko ek option dena chahiye. Aap jab salary paate ho next week, tab aap atleast partial payment kar sakte ho na? Maybe Rs. 10,000 ya 12,000? Phir baaki aap next month mein kar denge?

Customer: Uh, 10,000? Woh bhi... <interruption> that's still quite a bit when the hospital bills are... aap nahi samajhte, Priya. Every day hospital mein alag-alag charges aate hain. Drips, medicines, specialist fees... I'm literally drowning. But okay, okay, let me think. Maybe... maybe Rs. 8,000 I can manage after salary comes. Baaki ke liye... I'll figure out kisi tarah.

Agent: Sir, Rs. 8,000 toh theek hai. Toh aap mujhe ek commitment de sakte ho na? Jab salary aayega 20th ke aas-paas, tab aap Rs. 8,000 pay kar denge? Aur baaki ke Rs. 10,500 ke liye aap next month tak time lo?

Customer: Haan, haan, aap theek kah rahe ho. 20th ko jab salary aayegi, main pehle hospital ka kuch bill clear karunga, aur phir Rs. 8,000 aapko dedicate karunga. That's... that's a promise. But Priya, please, ek baat aur. Agar mere paas agle mahine tak kuch situation aur serious ho jaye, toh aap mujhe call mat karna, okay? <interruption> I mean, not like that, but... please be understanding.

Agent: Sir, haan, bilkul. Main aapko 25th ko ek reminder de dungi, theek hai? Aur sir, agar aapko kisi aur cheez ke liye help chahiye, ya agar aapki wife theek ho jaye aur aap jaldi payment kar sakte ho, toh aap mujhe directly message kar sakte ho. Mere number note kar lo.

Customer: Okay, okay, thank you. Main samajhta hoon. Aur haan, mujhe hope hai ki next month tak meri wife theek ho jayegi aur main pehle se zyada payment kar dunga. Abhi toh bas yeh 8,000 confirm karo, aur main try karunga.

Agent: Perfect, sir. Toh aapka commitment Rs. 8,000 by 25th of this month, theek hai? Aur sir, mujhe aapki wife ke liye best wishes. Jaldi theek ho jaye.

Customer: Thank you, thank you, Priya. Main appreciate karta hoon aapki understanding. Aur haan, mujhe call mat karo ek hafte mein, please? Let me handle this crisis first.

Agent: Bilkul, sir. Take care, aur all the best.

transcript:
Agent: Namaste, main Rajesh bol raha hoon XYZ Finance se. Kya main Vikram Singh se baat kar sakta hoon?

Customer: Haan, main hi hoon. Lekin mujhe pata hai aap log kyun call kar rahe ho.

Agent: Vikram bhai, aapka account humara paas 47 din se overdue hai. EMI amount tha 18,500 rupees jo August mein due tha. Aaj tak payment nahi mila. Kya aap abhi payment kar sakte hain ya phir kab tak kar denge?

Customer: Dekho, main pehle se tum logon se baat kar chuka hoon. Mere paas abhi paise nahi hain aur na hi mujhe koi commitment deni hai. Agar tum log mujhe call karte raho to main apne lawyer ko bulaunga.

Agent: <interruption> Vikram sir, lawyer se kya lena-dena? Hum sirf aapka outstanding balance collect karna chahte hain. Agar aap promise kar den ki next week tak payment kar denge to hum—

Customer: Next week? Tum suno, main ne tumhare company ko pehle se likha tha ki mere account mein galti hai. Mujhe 18,500 nahi balki 12,000 hi dena chahiye. Tum log ne extra charges lagaye hain jo galat hain. Aur agar mujhe legal notice milta hai to main insolvency proceedings shuru kar dunga apne against mein.

Agent: Sir, insolvency... main samajh raha hoon. Lekin pehle aapka amount dispute settle karte hain. Aapka statement check karte hain—

Customer: <interruption> Statement? Main tumhare paas statement bhejna nahi chahta. Mujhe sirf itna kehna hai — mera lawyer ab mere saath hai aur agar koi aur call aaye to hum counter-action lenge. Aapko sirf legal team se baat karnani chahiye, mera lawyer se. Samjha?

Agent: Sir, I understand your concern. Lekin kya aap apne lawyer ke naam aur contact details de sakte ho so that we can coordinate?

Customer: Nahi. Aur na hi main koi payment karunga jab tak ye amount dispute resolve nahi hota. Tum logon ne mujhe overcharge kiya hai aur main iska jawab dene ko tayyar hoon. RBI ko complaint bhi likh sakta hoon agar tumne harassment jaari rakhni hai. Do not call me again.

Agent: Sir, I understand. Lekin kripya—

Customer: <interruption> Kripya kya? Bas mat call karo. Main serious hoon.

[Call Disconnected]

transcript:
Agent: Hello, good afternoon! Am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar? This is Priya calling from Infinity Finance regarding your loan account.

Customer: Haan, main Rajesh bol raha hoon. But listen, I don't have time for this. Aap logon ne pichle do hafte mein itne calls kiye hain... <interruption> I'm in the middle of something.

Agent: Rajesh ji, I understand you're busy. This will just take two minutes. Your account with us — loan reference number IL-2847-56 — shows an outstanding balance of 84,500 rupees. The payment was due on the 15th of this month, and we haven't received it yet. Can we discuss—

Customer: <overlapping> Dekho, that amount is wrong. Mujhe pata hai main kitna owe karta hoon. Aap logon ne interest aur penalties lagaya hain jo bilkul galat hain. Maine jo original loan tha uska amount 75,000 tha. Bas yeh extra charges maine approve nahi kiye.

Agent: I appreciate you clarifying that, Rajesh. Let me explain — the interest accrual is as per the loan agreement terms which you signed. The penalty was applied because your September payment bounced. But let's focus on getting this resolved. Can you make a payment of at least 40,000 by tomorrow? We can work out the remaining amount after that.

Customer: Arre, no no no. Main kuch bhi nahi dene wala. Mujhe pata hai yeh sab scam hai. Aap logon ne mujhe galat tarike se convince kiya tha jab loan diya tha. Mere liye yeh legitimate nahi hai, samajhte ho? <pause> And frankly, I don't want any more calls. Don't call me again.

Agent: Rajesh, I hear your frustration, but we need to resolve this. Your account is now 47 days overdue. If we don't get a commitment from you, this will escalate to our legal team. Can we at least discuss a settlement option where you pay less than the full amount?

Customer: <voice rising> Nahi. Main nahi dene wala. Kuch bhi mat bolo. Maine already socha hai — agar aap log dobara call karoge, toh main RBI ko complaint karunga. Aur social media par bhi post karunga how your company harassed me. Main serious hoon. Bas stop calling me. <interruption> I'm hanging up now.

Agent: Rajesh, please don't hang up. Let me escalate this to my supervisor who might be able to offer you better terms—

Customer: <disconnecting> Nahi. Finished. No more calls. Bye.

transcript:
Agent: Namaste, kya main Priya Sharma se baat kar sakta hoon? This is Rajesh from XYZ Finance, regarding your loan account number 4521-8847-9.

Customer: Haan, main hi Priya bol rahi hoon... but, uh, kaun bola aapka naam?

Agent: Rajesh, ma'am. Main aapke account ke baare mein call kar raha hoon. Aapke paas outstanding balance hai rupees 1,43,500 jo last month se pending hai. Due date tha 15th September. Kya aap abhi payment kar sakte hain?

Customer: <interruption> Haan haan, I know, I know... but mujhe... mujhe ek minute do na. Mera dimag thoda confuse hai aaj. Main... main kya bol rahi tha?

Agent: Ma'am, aapka payment — 1,43,500 rupees. Aapne pichle mahine kuch kaha tha ki September ke end mein de denge?

Customer: Haan, that's right... but Rajesh, I... main abhi thik se soch nahi pa rahi. Mera head bahut heavy feel ho raha hai. Kya aap baad mein call kar sakte ho? Shayad kal main theek se baat kar paunga.

Agent: Ma'am, bas ek minute. Kya aap theek hain? Aapke voice mein kahin kuch... are you okay?

Customer: <interruption> Nahi, I mean... haan, I'm fine, I'm fine... just thoda tired. Aur maine ek aur loan bhi le rakha hai HDFC se... woh EMI bhi deni padti hai na, aur pati ne bola tha ki pehle uska payment karo... uska due date 10th ko tha. So I'm just... I don't know, Rajesh. Sab kuch bahut heavy lag raha hai.

Agent: Ma'am, understood. Aapke paas multiple loans hain. But this one is with us, and it's quite overdue now. Can you give me a date when you can pay?

Customer: <interruption> Date? Haan... maybe... maybe next week? But I'm not sure. Pati mujhe samjhate hain na ki main kya karo, kya na karo. He says your company wale bahut aggressive hain, calling bahut zyada. Is it true? Aur maine kuch din pehle RBI ko bhi suna tha... ki agar koi aggressive calling kare to complain kar sakte ho?

Agent: Ma'am, we follow all RBI guidelines. But tell me, has someone been rude to you on previous calls?

Customer: Nahi nahi, you're not rude. But I'm just... I'm scared, Rajesh. Main samajh nahi pa rahi ki main kya karo. Pati ne kaha tha ki settle kar do, ya kuch aur option dekho. But I'm confused. Aur mera mental health bhi theek nahi hai... I've been taking medicines for anxiety. Aaj ka din bahut bad tha.

Agent: <interruption> Ma'am, I... I understand. Let me just note this down. You mentioned your husband is managing the finances. Is he available right now to speak?

Customer: Nahi, he's at work. He comes home around 8-9 PM. But Rajesh, I don't want him to get angry again. Last time when the agent called, he... he shouted at me, said why am I not managing this properly. <long pause> Sorry, I shouldn't be telling you this.

Agent: Ma'am, it's okay. But I need to understand — are you safe right now? Is everything alright at home?

Customer: <interruption> Haan haan, I'm fine. Just... just stressed. Loan ka pressure, family ka pressure. Maine ek din kahna bhi chaaha ki nahi, iss din se main kuch nahi pay kar sakti, but then... I got scared. Kyunki pati ko agar pata chale, to... <trails off>

Agent: Ma'am, I'm hearing some concern in your voice. Let me tell you something — we are going to pause all collection calls on your account for now. I am flagging your account as needing specialist support. You need to speak with someone who can understand what you're going through, not just about the money.

Customer: <interruption> Matlab? What do you mean pause? Aur kya hoga loan ka?

Agent: The loan won't go anywhere, ma'am. But we will not call you repeatedly. Instead, a trained counselor from our team will reach out to you — maybe after a few days — and they will speak with you about options that work for your situation. Aapko time denge. And if you feel unsafe or very stressed at any point, please reach out to us. There are helplines too, for people who are experiencing anxiety or stress at home.

Customer: <interruption> Helpline? <nervous laugh> Nahi nahi, I don't need helpline. Pati ko agar pata chale...

Agent: Ma'am, this is confidential. No one needs to know except you and our team. But your health and safety come first, before any payment. Samajhti ho?

Customer: <long pause> Haan... haan, I understand. Thank you. Ek baat aur — aap mere husband ko call mat karna, haan? Bas mujhe hi call karna.

Agent: Absolutely, ma'am. Only you. Aur ek contact number update kar do — agar ye number change ho to naya number de dena. But main mark kar dunga ki sirf aapko call karna, aur wo bhi gentle way mein, theek?

Customer: Theek hai. Thank you, Rajesh. Main... main try karunga thik hone ke liye.

Agent: Bilkul, ma'am. Take care of yourself. Aapka account now flagged as — vulnerability case with priority counselor support. Aur ma'am, agar kisi din urgent help chahiye, to please call us back, haan?

Customer: Haan, thank you.

Customer: Theek hai, main abhi kar leta hoon transfer. Paise hain mere paas, bas yeh technical issues hain na frustrating. Agar isme bhi problem aaye, toh main zarur call karunga kal.

Agent: Bilkul. IMPS generally reliable hota hai. Kal morning ko call kar dena agar issue aaye. Aur Rajesh, teri willingness to dikhta hai payment karne ki — yeh achha hai.

Customer: Theek hai bhai, main try kar leta hoon. Agar successful ho gaya toh acha, aur nahi toh kal contact karunga.

Customer: Haan, main hi hoon. Kya baat hai?

Agent: Rajesh bhai, aapke paas ek loan account hai jo hamara records mein active dikhai de raha hai. Account number 4521-8367-XXXX, jo September mein due tha. Outstanding amount 56,200 rupees hai. Aapne abhi payment nahi kiya.

Customer: Kaunsa Rajesh? Sunao, main toh Rajesh Patel hoon, aur main Mumbai mein rahta hoon. Aapka account number galat lag raha hai mujhe.

Agent: Theek hai, par Sector 5 Ghaziabad mein kisi Rajesh Kumar ko jaante ho?

Customer: <interruption> Nahi nahi, main Mumbai se hoon. Mera naam Rajesh Patel hai. Agar koi Rajesh Kumar Ghaziabad mein hai toh woh main nahi hoon.

Agent: Acha, par batao — kya tumne kabhi HDFC Finance se koi loan liya hai?

Customer: Haan, ek loan tha par woh toh mere bhai ke naam tha. Mere bhai Suresh ke naam tha, jo ab nahi raha. Woh 2018 mein liya tha, par mujhe lagta hai woh band ho gaya hoga.

Agent: Toh aap Rajesh ho, par loan Suresh ke naam tha?

Customer: Haan, confusion ho gaya. Main... main toh sirf usi ke liye responsible nahi hoon. Woh toh mere bhai ka loan tha.

Agent: Theek hai, Rajesh bhai, par mujhe ek baat suspicious lag rahi hai. Aapke paas jo phone number hai, woh mere system mein ek aur account ke saath linked hai. Dono accounts default mein hain, aur dono ke paas same mobile number pehle tha. Kya aap batayenge ki aapne yeh number kaise share kiya dusre account holders ke saath?

Customer: Kya matlab? Ek hi number do accounts ke liye? Yeh toh... yeh toh galat hai na. Main toh bas ek loan jaanta hoon, aur woh bhi mere bhai ka tha.

Agent: Suresh, main aapko ek important baat batana chahta hoon. Aapne pehle apna naam Rajesh Patel kaha, ab kya kah rahe ho?

Customer: Haan, main Rajesh hoon, par mere bhai Suresh ke loan ke baare mein baat kar raha tha. Confusion mein...

Agent: Dekho, yeh identity mismatch bilkul clear hai. Aapne pehle Rajesh Patel kaha, phir Suresh ke naam ka loan liya, aur ab yeh bhi nahi batana chahte identity confirm karne ke liye. Aur dono accounts same number se linked hain. Mujhe lagta hai yeh fraud ka signal hai.

Customer: <interruption> Fraud? Main toh kuch galat nahi kiya. Mujhe pata hi nahi tha ki mere bhai ka loan abhi active hai.

Agent: Theek hai, par account ke records batate hain ki yeh number do alag accounts ke saath pehle se linked tha. Yeh pattern fraud investigation ki zaroorat hai. Main ab aapka case escalate kar raha hoon fraud team ko, aur aapka account immediately suppress ho jayega. Aapko legal team se baat karna padega.

Customer: Sunao, mujhe kya karna hai? Main toh bas—

Agent: Abhi aapko kuch karna nahi hai. Fraud investigation mein account block hoga, aur legal team aapse contact karega. Aapne identity confirm nahi kiya, aur multiple accounts same number se linked hain — yeh serious matter hai.

Customer: Theek hai.
L3: Identity Inconsistency on Call – Fraud Signal|Identity Unconfirmed – Verification Refused or Failed|Loan Taken by Deceased Relative|Claims Loan Was Closed / NOC Issued|Fraud Signal – Identity Inconsistency on Call

transcript:
Agent: Namaste Rajesh ji, aap se baat kar raha hoon Abhishek se, collections team se. Aapka EMI 15th ko due tha na, abhi tak payment nahi aaya. Kya sab theek hai?

Customer: Haan haan, namaste. Dekhiye, mera account toh theek hai, par bank se ek problem hai. Mere savings account mein ek hold lag gaya hai kuch din pehle.

Agent: Hold? Matlab kya hua? Aapne to kuch galat transaction kiya kya?

Customer: Nahi nahi, mera kuch nahi hua. Actually, mere account mein ek court order aa gaya tha, RBI ke compliance ke liye. Bank ne kaha ki mere account ko freeze kar diya gaya hai until investigation complete ho jaaye.

Agent: <interruption>Court order? Kaunsa court order, Rajesh?</interruption>

Customer: Arre, mujhe properly pata nahi. Bank ne bas kaha ki ek lien lag gayi hai mujhe account pe, kisi regulatory case ke wajah se. Unhone mujhe letter diya tha approximately 10 din pehle. Maine try kiya UPI se paise nikalne ke liye, nahi ho paya. Net banking se debit karne ki koshish ki, wo bhi nahi hua.

Agent: Toh aap bolna chahte ho ki aap payment karna chahte ho, par bank account se nahi kar sakte abhi?

Customer: Bilkul. Mera intent toh bilkul clear hai. Mere paas funds hain, par account lock hai. Iska matlab mujhe 10-15 din wait karna padega jab tak bank apna investigation complete kar le.

Agent: Samajh gaya. Toh aap apna outstanding amount batayein — 45,000 rupees hai na?

Customer: Haan, 45,000 theek hai, par interest charges mein kuch doubt hai. Mujhe lagta hai extra charges lag gaye hain. But pehle toh account unlock karna padega.

Agent: Theek hai. Toh aap bank se contact kar liye ho aur poocha hai ki kab tak unlock hoga?

Customer: Haan, unhone kaha 7-10 din aur lag jayenge. Unka investigation department abhi process kar raha hai. Unhone bola ki meri ID aur address verify ho gaya, bas final clearance baaki hai.

Agent: <interruption>Toh aap mujhe callback de sakte ho na 12 din baad jab account unlock ho jaye?</interruption>

Customer: Haan, 12 din mein aap call karo. Tab tak bank ka process complete ho jayega. Aur mujhe alternate payment channel diya jaa sakta hai kya? Cheque se de sakta hoon ya branch mein cash deposit kar sakta hoon?

Agent: Bilkul. Aap NEFT se bhi kar sakte ho, ya phir branch mein jaa kar cash deposit kar sakte ho. Mujhe aapka address confirm karna hai — aap Mumbai mein rehte ho na, Andheri West?

Customer: Haan haan, same address. Par ek cheez aur — bank ne kaha ki mere account pe lien hai, toh mere savings account se transfer nahi hoga. Cheque bhi ussi account se to draw hona padega na?

Agent: Aah, samajh gaya. Toh cash deposit hi theek rahe. Aap branch mein jaa kar directly 45,000 deposit kar sakte ho, cheque receipt le sakte ho, aur hume WhatsApp ya email se receipt send kar sakte ho.

Customer: Theek hai. Par mujhe aapka ek aur chiz batani hai — ek dusre lender ka 8,000 rupees ka EMI bhi same date mein tha, aur woh default pad gaya. Mera paisa sab jagah spread hai.

Agent: Samajh gaya, par abhi humare 45,000 pe focus karte hain. 12 din baad jab account unlock ho jaye, aap branch mein deposit kar dena. Theek hai?

Customer: Bilkul. 12 din baad bank se mujhe clear confirmation mil jayega, tab mein immediately deposit kar dunga. Aur agar account unlock ho jaye toh UPI se bhi kar sakta hoon.

Agent: Perfect. Toh main aapka follow-up call schedule kar dunga 12th din ke liye. Aapka current number yeh hai na, 98xxxxxx00?

Customer: Haan, yeh number theek hai. Aur agar main early deposit kar sakta hoon toh kar dunga, par 12 din ke andar toh definitely kar dunga.

Agent: Bilkul. Aapka account hold ka status mujhe note kar dunga aur legal team ko notify kar dunga taaki koi aur pressure na ho. Aap apne bank ke investigation process ko follow karte rahna.

Customer: Shukriya yaar. Aapne samajh liya meri situation ko. Mujhe pata hai mera debt hai, par account lock hai toh kya kar sakta hoon?

Agent: Bilkul samajh gaya. Aap bank se ek written confirmation le lena jab account unlock ho jaye, aur hume send kar dena. Theek hai?

Customer: Haan, zaroor. Thank you. 12 din baad call karna yaad rakhna.

Agent: Pakka. Take care, Rajesh.

transcript:
Agent: Namaste, good afternoon. Am I speaking with Rajesh Sharma?

Customer: Yes, speaking. Who is this? I'm in the middle of something.

Agent: Sir, this is Priya from the Collections team at FinanceHub. I'm calling regarding your loan account ending in 4782. You have an outstanding EMI of rupees 18,500 due since the 15th of this month. Can we discuss your payment status?

Customer: Look, I know about the EMI. But this is the fourth call I've received this week. Four calls! From different people saying the same thing. I don't appreciate being harassed like this.

Agent: Sir, I understand your frustration. However, we do need to resolve this matter. The account is now 18 days overdue. If you could commit to a payment date—

Customer: <interruption> Commit? I've already explained everything to the last three people who called. Why do I have to repeat myself again and again? This is not fair.

Agent: I sincerely apologize for the repeated calls, sir. That shouldn't have happened. But looking at your account, I see we're now approaching the escalation stage. I need to understand — can you make the payment this week?

Customer: The thing is, my salary is delayed. It should come by the 28th. But that's not the main issue here. The main issue is that I'm being treated like a criminal. I received a call yesterday at 6:45 PM — that's after your business hours, correct? And the person was very rude to me. He said things like, "You're going to ruin your credit, you'll never get a loan again." That's not how you should speak to a customer.

Agent: Sir, that is completely unacceptable. I apologize on behalf of the agent. We have strict guidelines about respectful communication. Can I take note of the agent's name or the time of that call?

Customer: I don't remember the name. It was yesterday evening. But here's what I want — I don't want to deal with this over the phone anymore. I want everything in writing. I want a proper letter from your manager or someone senior explaining the situation, the charges, everything. And I want to respond in writing. I'm not comfortable with these phone calls anymore. This whole process feels unprofessional.

Agent: I completely understand, sir. Given what you've experienced, that's a fair request. Let me escalate this to my supervisor and our grievance cell right away. They will prepare a formal written communication with a detailed account statement and settlement options. You'll receive that within 2 business days.

Customer: And I want someone senior to review this. Not just any grievance cell. I want a manager or a senior officer to look at my account, because frankly, I'm also not sure about some of the charges that have been added. The penalty seems very high for just a few days of delay. So I want that reviewed as well before I commit to anything.

Agent: Sir, that's a valid concern. When you escalate to the senior team, they will also conduct a comprehensive review of all charges — interest, penalties, everything — and they will include that in the written communication. Is there anything else I should note for the escalation?

Customer: Yes. My new contact number is 9876543210. The old one is giving issues. Please update that. And I want confirmation that no more calls will be made to me until I receive the written communication from your senior management. Is that clear?

Agent: Absolutely clear, sir. I'm updating your contact number to 9876543210 right now. And I'm putting a note on your account — no outbound calls until the senior team's written communication is sent. You have my word on that. Your escalation reference number is ESC-2024-891456. Please keep that for your records.

Customer: Okay. And one more thing — make sure they send it by email as well, not just by post. I want it digitally too.

Agent: Noted, sir. Both email and postal communication. You should expect the escalation package within 2 business days. Is there anything else?

Customer: No, that's all. Thank you for listening, at least. I hope the senior team handles this better.

Agent: Thank you for your patience, sir. We will absolutely ensure this is handled properly at the senior level. You will hear from us soon. Have a good day.
L3: Complains of Excessive Call Frequency|Complains of Calls Outside Permitted Hours|Complains of Rude / Abusive Agent Behaviour|Disputes Interest / Penalty Charges|Salary Delayed – Awaiting Credit|Contact Number Updated – New Number Shared|Identity Confirmed – Borrower Verified on Call

Customer: Sir, Papa ko stress nahi de sakte. Doctor ne strictly kaha hai ki unhe tension nahi dena. Main hi sab handle karunga. Aap directly mujhe hi contact karo aage se.

Agent: Theek hai Arjun. Main iska case immediately bereavement aur incapacity team ko pass kar dunga. Wo aapko 2-3 din mein contact karenge aur permanent solution nikaalenge. Tab tak aap tension mat lo. Aur agar urgent kuch ho, toh mujhe call kar dena.

Agent: Haan, main apna extension aapko SMS kar dunga. Aur Arjun, bahut brave ho tum. Papa theek ho jayenge, yeh dua hai.

Customer: Dhanyavaad sir.

Customer: Khuda hafiz sir.

Agent: I see. So you are saying the payment was made on the 8th, but it's not reflecting in our system or in the bureau report. Have you received any confirmation from your bank for that payment?

Customer: Yes, yes, I have the UPI reference number. It is <interruption> wait, let me find it. The reference is UPI20231208XXXXX4782. I have the screenshot also. The money went out from my account, madam. I can show you. But why is the bureau still showing me as defaulter? This is affecting my credit score. I cannot take any new loan like this.

Agent: Understood, Rajesh. That's frustrating. Let me note down this reference number. We will verify this payment against our records. But I must ask — before we proceed, can you help me confirm your current address? Is it still 42-B, Lakshmi Nagar, Jaipur?

Customer: Haan, that is correct. But madam, the main issue is the bureau reporting. Until you correct the bureau records and remove the default mark, I don't want to make another payment. How can I pay again when my name is already spoiled in the bureau? First you correct the records, then I will clear anything that is still pending.

Agent: I hear you. The bureau reporting is definitely important. However, I need to clarify — our records here also show the account as overdue. So even if the payment on the 8th was made, we haven't received it in our system yet. It could be in transit or there could be a technical issue. Let me escalate this to our verification team today itself.

Customer: But why is this happening? I am not a person who doesn't pay, madam. I have always paid on time. This EMI was due on the 5th, and I paid on the 8th. That is only three days late. And now you are calling me as if I am some big defaulter. The bureau should not show me like this.

Agent: You're right, and I apologize for the concern. The good news is that we can investigate this. Once we verify the payment using the reference number you provided, we will request the credit bureau to correct the reporting immediately. This is a standard process. Once we confirm your payment, the correction to the bureau will happen automatically after we update our system. The bureau mirrors our records. So the sequence is: we verify and confirm receipt, we update our system, and then within 5-7 working days, the bureau report will reflect the correction.

Customer: Okay, okay. But I want this in writing. I want an email or something confirming that you are investigating this and that the bureau will be corrected. I cannot just trust on a phone call. Too many problems already.

Agent: That's absolutely fair. I will send you an email today with the case reference number and the escalation details. Agent: Good afternoon, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Yes, this is Rajesh. Who is calling?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Priya from Axis Finance collections. I'm calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 4782. Do you have a few minutes to speak?

Customer: Haan, yes, I know about this. What is it about now? I've already made the last payment.

Agent: Thank you for confirming. I'm calling because your account shows a due amount of 47,500 rupees for the last two months — August and September. Our records show the payment is now 62 days overdue. Can you help me understand what happened?

Customer: Sixty-two days? No, no, wait. I made a payment of 18,000 in early August. The EMI is 23,750 per month, so... <interruption> I don't think I owe that much. Let me check my bank statement one minute.

Agent: Of course, take your time.

Customer: <pause> Okay, so I paid 18,000 on August 5th, but then my company had some restructuring. My salary got delayed in September — it came on the 25th instead of the usual date. So I missed that month. And October's EMI, I haven't paid yet because... well, Priya, the situation is quite difficult right now.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. Can you tell me more about the situation? Is the salary issue still ongoing, or has it been resolved?

Customer: The salary is back to normal now, but here's the problem. My company is going through some downsizing, and they've cut my salary by 15 percent. They said it's temporary, but I don't know how long it will last. And I have another loan — a car loan — with HDFC, and that EMI is 12,000 per month. So combined with your 23,750, I'm looking at almost 36,000 in EMIs every month. My take-home is now about 70,000, so after rent, groceries, and other expenses, I'm really struggling.

Agent: I see. That's a challenging situation. How much are you able to pay towards this account right now?

Customer: That's the thing — I can pay something, maybe 10,000 right now, but I cannot commit to 23,750 every month going forward. I just cannot. Even if I wanted to, it's not possible. I was thinking... is there any way you can reduce the EMI? Or maybe give me some months off? A moratorium, you know? Even for three months, that would help me get back on my feet.

Agent: That's a good question. Before I explore those options, let me confirm — you're saying you're unable to service both your EMIs at the current rate?

Customer: Exactly. I'm not refusing to pay — I want to pay, but I need the EMI to be lower. What if you could reduce it to, say, 15,000 per month? Or extend the loan tenure so the EMI comes down? I'm willing to work something out, but the current amount is impossible.

Agent: Understood. And the 10,000 you mentioned — when would you be able to pay that?

Customer: I can arrange that by the 15th of this month. My salary comes on the 1st, so after paying rent on the 5th and other essentials, I can have that ready.

Agent: Okay, Rajesh. What you're asking for — a reduction in EMI, a moratorium, or tenure extension — these are restructuring options that I cannot approve directly. But I absolutely understand your situation, and I want to help. I will need to escalate your case to my manager and our restructuring team. They will review your income documents, your other loan obligations, and come back to you with a formal proposal within 5 to 7 working days.

Customer: Okay, that sounds good. But I want to make sure this is actually going to happen, you know? I don't want to be stuck in the same situation after one week.

Agent: I completely understand your concern. To move this forward, I will need a few documents from you. Can you provide your latest salary slip and bank statements for the last three months? This will help our team assess your income and confirm the salary reduction you mentioned.

Customer: Yes, I can send those. But, um, one more thing — I also want to know if the penalty charges on this account can be waived. I know I've been late, but with the salary cut and everything, it's been very stressful. If those charges are removed, it would help a lot.

Agent: That's also something the restructuring team can look at. It's not something I can promise, but they may consider it as part of the overall relief package, depending on your income situation and the lender's policy. For now, let me log your request for EMI reduction, moratorium, and penalty waiver consideration.

Customer: Okay, thank you. So what happens next?

Agent: Next, I'll send you an email with a list of documents we need — salary slip, bank statements, and any proof of your other loan obligations. Once you submit those, our restructuring team will review everything and contact you within 5 to 7 days with a formal proposal. In the meantime, if you can arrange the 10,000 payment by the 15th, that would be helpful and show good faith.

Customer: Yes, I'll send the documents by tomorrow, and I'll make sure the payment goes through by the 15th. I really appreciate this, Priya. I was worried you would just tell me to pay the full amount or face legal action.

Agent: Not at all, Rajesh. We're here to work with you. I can see you're in a difficult situation, and you're willing to find a solution. That's what matters. I'll make a note that you're cooperating and that we're exploring restructuring options. Thank you for your time, and I'll make sure the team contacts you soon.

Customer: Thank you, Priya. I'll wait for their call.

Agent: You're welcome. Have a good day, Rajesh.

Customer: You too. Bye.

Agent: Namaste, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar? This is Ananya calling from Credix Finance regarding your loan account.

Agent: I understand, Mr. Kumar. But before we involve legal, let me clarify the situation. This is regarding your account LAC-4521089, the personal loan amount of Rs. 2,85,000, correct? Your EMI of Rs. 8,950 was due on the 15th of last month.

Customer: Haan, that account, but the problem is... I received a summons, sir. The court notice came, and my lawyer said don't talk to anyone without him present. I am very worried. What is happening? Why did they send a court notice?

Agent: Mr. Kumar, the legal notice was sent because your account has been in default for nearly 120 days now. We have been trying to reach you since June to understand the situation. But I can help you. Many customers in your position have resolved this without further court proceedings. Can you tell me what happened? Why couldn't you pay?

Customer: <interruption> No, no, but I... I don't have that much money right now. My business, you see, it had a problem. My supplier, he disappeared, and I lost almost everything. The stock was stuck. I have been trying to recover, but it is very difficult.

Agent: I see. So this is a temporary situation due to business disruption? How long do you think before you can get back on track?

Customer: Maybe two, three months. But sir, the court notice... my lawyer is saying the bank can take action against me. Can they do that? I am very scared. I have a family. Can we settle this before it goes further in court?

Agent: That's actually a very good question, and I'm glad you're asking. Yes, the court proceedings are active now, which means we need to handle this differently. But there is still a possibility. If you can demonstrate your willingness to resolve this, we can approach the legal team and request that they consider a settlement before the next hearing. What amount do you think you could manage in the next 30 days?

Customer: I... I don't know. The full amount is too much. Maybe I can arrange 50,000 or 60,000 in the next month? But I need to be honest, I may not be able to pay the full amount even after that.

Agent: Okay, that's helpful. A partial settlement is something we can explore, but since legal proceedings are already underway, I cannot make you any promises directly. What I will do is escalate your case to our legal team. They will review your situation and may contact you or your lawyer directly with settlement options. But Mr. Kumar, you must understand — because you have received a court summons, from this moment forward, this matter is being treated as a legal escalation. You should expect contact from our legal department.

Customer: <interruption> But will they stop calling me? Will they stop the court case if I settle?

Agent: That depends on what settlement amount the legal team approves and when you can pay it. If you settle, yes, the case can be withdrawn before the hearing. But I cannot promise that right now. What I can do is log your willingness to settle and your approximate capacity of 50,000 to 60,000 rupees, and forward this to the legal team. They will contact you within 3 to 5 business days.

Customer: Okay... okay, but my lawyer's number, should I give you that? Or should the bank's lawyers call my lawyer directly?

Agent: Your lawyer can reach out to us, or our legal team will try to contact you first. If you prefer, you can share the lawyer's contact, and we will ensure all future communication goes through them. What is the best number for the legal team to reach you?

Customer: My number is still the same. And my lawyer is Ashok Verma, his number is 98765-43210. Please tell them to call him, not me directly. I don't want any more calls to my mobile.

Agent: Perfect, Mr. Kumar. I have noted that. Ashok Verma, 98765-43210. Our legal team will reach out to him. I am also noting that you have indicated willingness to settle with a capacity of Rs. 50,000 to 60,000 within the next 30 days, and that your business disruption is the reason for non-payment. This file is now being escalated to our Legal and Escalations team. You can expect contact from them shortly. Is there anything else you need to tell me before I close this call?

Customer: Just... please, tell them to hurry. The next hearing is in two weeks. I want this resolved before that.

Agent: I will mark this as urgent. Thank you for your time and for being honest with me, Mr. Kumar. Goodbye.

Customer: Thank you. Goodbye.

Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Verma?

Customer: Haan, I know, I know about the EMI. Look, the thing is... I'm really struggling right now. It's not that I don't want to pay, but I have too many loans going on. There's the car loan, there's my wife's education loan with ICICI, and now this one. Every month it's EMI, EMI, EMI. <interruption> Sorry, sorry, one moment — beta, not now!

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. Let me help you here. Your monthly income is 65,000, correct? With the car loan EMI of 12,000 and this loan's EMI of 18,500, that's already 30,500 before your wife's education EMI. What is that amount?

Customer: Arey, that's 9,500. So altogether we're paying 40,000 every month just in EMIs. How am I supposed to manage? <interruption> Sorry, sorry, my wife is asking about something. Look, the remaining 25,000 I have, I have to pay rent, electricity, groceries, children's school fees. There's nothing left. And last month, I had to prioritise the car loan because the bank was threatening to repossess the car. So I couldn't pay you.

Agent: I see. So you made a choice to pay the car EMI first because of the repossession threat?

Customer: Yes, exactly. The car is essential for my work. I'm a delivery supervisor, I need the car. But I cannot pay all three loans at the same time. It's impossible. The numbers don't work out.

Agent: Rajesh, I hear you. This is a genuine situation of overindebtedness. Tell me, what would you like to do? Can you commit to paying this 2,14,500 in full, or would you prefer to explore other options?

Customer: What options? Can you reduce the EMI? Can you give me a moratorium for two or three months so I can catch up? Because once I settle the car loan in another four months, I'll have more breathing room. After that, I can pay this one more comfortably.

Agent: That's a good plan. But for now, can you at least commit to paying the overdue amount of 18,500 for this month? Even a partial payment would help us move forward.

Customer: <interruption> Haan, I can try. But honestly, even that is difficult right now. My salary just came, 65,000, but I've already mentally allocated it to the car and the education loan. Maybe I can find 5,000 to 7,000 for you by next week. Can I do that?

Agent: Rajesh, I understand you're in a tight spot. A partial commitment of 5,000 to 7,000 would at least show good faith. But I must inform you that without a clear restructure approval from my manager, I cannot promise a moratorium or EMI reduction. What I can do is escalate your case for a hardship assessment based on your overindebtedness situation.

Customer: Haan, please do that. Because I want to pay, I really do. But I cannot pay 40,000 in EMIs every month on a 65,000 salary. It's just not possible. I'm not refusing to pay — I'm just being realistic about what I can manage.

Agent: Understood, Rajesh. Let me document this clearly. You're committing to pay 5,000 to 7,000 towards the overdue amount by next Friday, the 29th, yes?

Agent: I'll include that request in the escalation. For now, I'm marking your account for hardship assessment and internal restructure review. A senior team member will contact you within two working days with the outcome.

Customer: Thank you. And please, no more calls until you have something concrete to offer. I'm stressed enough as it is.

Agent: Noted, Rajesh. We'll be in touch. Thank you for being upfront about your situation.

Agent: Hello, good morning. Am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Yes, this is Rajesh speaking. Who is this?

Customer: Yeah, I have a couple of minutes. What is this about? I've been making payments, no?

Agent: Thank you for taking my call. I can see your account here. Your current outstanding balance is rupees 87,450, and it's been 45 days overdue now. The last payment we received was on the 15th of October. Can you help me understand what's happened?

Customer: Forty-five days? That doesn't sound right. I paid that amount already. I made a payment in November itself. Check your system properly.

Agent: I understand your concern, Rajesh. Let me pull up the payment history here. I see the payment from November was received and adjusted, yes. But there's still an outstanding of 87,450 remaining. The issue here is the account is showing on your credit bureau report as defaulted now. That's why I'm calling.

Customer: Wait, wait. My credit report? How can they say I'm defaulted when I've been paying regularly? This is wrong. The bank is showing wrong information to CIBIL.

Agent: I can understand your frustration. Can you tell me more about what you mean? What information do you think is incorrect?

Customer: The outstanding amount they are showing is too high. I calculated it myself — I paid 20,000 in September, 35,000 in October, and 25,000 in November. That's 80,000 rupees I paid already. So why are they showing 87,450? And on top of that, they added some penalty charges that I never agreed to. The bureau is showing all this wrong information because your system is not updating correctly.

Agent: Okay, I hear you. So you're saying the amount shown in the credit bureau is inflated because of penalties and possibly because payments are not being reflected correctly?

Customer: Exactly! And I want this corrected in CIBIL before I make any more payments. How can I pay if my credit report is already damaged by wrong information? First, you people fix the reporting. Show the correct amount owed, remove these penalty charges that shouldn't be there, and then I will pay. I'm not defaulting — your system is the problem here.

Agent: I completely understand your position, Rajesh. This is a serious concern. Let me be clear about what I'm hearing — you're disputing the accuracy of how your account has been reported to the credit bureau, and you want the bureau records corrected before you proceed with any payment. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, that's exactly what I'm saying. I'm a responsible person. I've never missed a payment in my life before this. And now you're telling the bureau I'm a defaulter because of wrong calculations and penalties I didn't authorize? This is unfair.

Agent: I understand completely. This requires verification at our end. I'm going to escalate this to our accounts team to cross-check your payment records against what's been reported to CIBIL. We'll need to audit the penalties applied and confirm the exact outstanding amount.

Customer: How long will this take? And what happens in the meantime? Do I just wait?

Agent: Good question. Once I escalate this, our team will review it within 5 to 7 working days. In the meantime, I would request you not to make any payment until we've verified the figures. Once we've confirmed what the correct amount is, we'll contact you with an update and a corrected statement.

Customer: Okay, but I'm telling you now — if CIBIL is still showing this wrong information next week, I'm going to file a complaint with the RBI about this. This is not right.

Agent: I completely understand your frustration, and I assure you we'll prioritize this review. I'm noting your concern about the bureau reporting in the system right now. Can I get your email address to send you a summary of what we've discussed today?

Customer: It's rajesh.kumar.2891@mailbox.com. Please make sure you get back to me. And please tell your team to correct this in CIBIL. I don't want my credit score damaged because of your system error.

Agent: I've noted that, Rajesh. Your email is rajesh.kumar.2891@mailbox.com. I'm logging this as a bureau reporting dispute with a priority review flag. Our accounts and compliance team will contact you within 7 days with an update. Is there anything else I should note before I close this call?

Customer: Just make sure you fix it. That's all I'm asking.

Agent: Absolutely. Thank you for your time, Rajesh. We'll be in touch very soon.
